events.title: Æthelstan receives the submission of northern rulers at Eamont
events.description: At Eamont, near Penrith, four rulers, among them King Constantine II of Alba, King Hywel Dda of Deheubarth and Ealdred of Bamburgh, accepted Æthelstan's overlordship. Seven years of peace in the north followed.

events.title: Acre surrenders to the armies of the Third Crusade
events.description: After a siege of almost two years, the garrison of Acre surrendered to Richard I and Philip II. The port became the crusaders' main base and later capital of the Kingdom of Jerusalem.

events.title: Pope Benedict XII issues a bull to reform the Cistercians
events.description: At Sorgues, Pope Benedict XII issued the bull Fulgens sicut stella matutina to reform the Cistercian Order. It prescribed economic consolidation of indebted houses, compulsory attendance at the general chapter, stricter discipline and reorganised theological studies for monks.

events.title: The Ottomans capture Negroponte and the island of Euboea
events.description: Sultan Mehmed II personally led the Ottoman siege of Negroponte (Chalcis), capital of the Venetian possession of Euboea. After almost a month, and despite heavy losses, the Ottomans took both the city and the island.

events.title: Henry VIII marries Catherine Parr, his sixth wife
events.description: Henry VIII married the twice-widowed Catherine Parr at Hampton Court. She outlived him, helped reconcile the king with his daughters and became the first English queen to publish a book in her own name.
events.html: Henry VIII married the twice-widowed Catherine Parr at Hampton Court. She outlived him, helped reconcile the king with his daughters and became the first English queen to publish a book in her own name.

events.title: Williamite army wins the Battle of Aughrim
events.description: William III's forces under Godert de Ginkel defeated the Jacobite army at Aughrim in County Galway (12 July Old Style). The bloodiest battle in Irish history effectively decided the Williamite war.

events.title: Lincoln signs the act creating the Army Medal of Honor
events.description: President Lincoln signed a resolution authorising the Medal of Honor for army soldiers who distinguished themselves by gallantry. It remains the highest US military decoration.
events.html: President Lincoln signed a resolution authorising the Medal of Honor for army soldiers who distinguished themselves by gallantry. It remains the highest US military decoration.

events.title: Soviet and German tanks clash at Prokhorovka
events.description: Soviet tank armies counter-attacked the SS Panzer Corps at Prokhorovka, one of the largest tank battles in history. The Soviets lost heavily, but the German offensive at Kursk was halted.

events.title: Malala Yousafzai is born in Pakistan's Swat Valley
events.description: Malala Yousafzai was born in Mingora. Shot by the Taliban in 2012 for campaigning for girls' education, she survived and in 2014 became the youngest Nobel Peace Prize laureate.
